Morwani et al. arXiv 2311.07568v2, Theorem 7 (m>=4(p-1), gamma*=sqrt(2/27)/(p^{1/2}(p-1))), and App. F.3 (Lemma 6 gives f=F(a,b)+lambda 1[a+b=c], so every frequency has the same diagonal amplitude) were both read in the PDF text. ICLR 2024 spotlight confirmed. Li et al. Theorem 4.1 (gamma*=2(k!)/((2k+2)^{(k+1)/2}(p-1)p^{(k-1)/2}), every frequency used) was read in the PMLR PDF. PMLR v258 pp.523-531 confirmed. I checked the algebra myself: n! B_p p/(p-1) equals Li's gamma* (ratio 1 to 1e-16 for p in {5,7,113} and n in {2..5}). An LP solve of Gamma_1 at p=5,7,113 gives p/(p-1) with a flat maximizer. The app:dense uniqueness proof is correct. Mathematics-lens addition: the Gamma_1 lemma, uniqueness included, is itself classical. With x_delta=(sqrt(y_j)cos(2pi j delta/p), sqrt(y_j)sin(...)), ||x_0-x_delta||^2=2 sum_j y_j kappa_j(delta), so Gamma_1 is the best minimum distance of a p-point cyclic group code on the sphere. The averaging step is the Rankin simplex bound, ||sum x_delta||^2>=0 => max <x_0,x_delta> >= -1/(p-1). Equality means a regular simplex, whose circulant Gram matrix forces flat Fourier weights. So even the 'explicit uniqueness' that the checker credited as new is a textbook fact. Only the framing (dense endpoint = s=1 member of a family that is sparse for s>1) is new. Suggest a one-line remark in app:dense. The Rankin page was fetched and its bib fields confirmed, but the theorem text was not visible, so no theorem number is given.
